summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with groin pain and an empty Foley catheter bag, which resolved upon sitting up. Evaluation revealed no urinary tract infection despite a positive initial urinalysis; repeat testing and culture indicated colonization rather than infection, so antibiotics were avoided. Left leg redness and swelling were assessed with ultrasound, which ruled out DVT, and findings were consistent with stasis dermatitis. His chronic right heel pressure ulcer showed no signs of infection and required only continued wound care. He remained stable throughout the admission, with no evidence of sepsis or cardiac decompensation. Blood cultures remained negative. He was discharged home with services, on unchanged home medications except for an increase in lisinopril to 5 mg daily, and with clear instructions on catheter care and when to seek medical attention.
problems: Mechanical complication due to urethral (indwelling) catheter
